title: Psalms Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Psalms 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust
Let the enemy persecute my soul
Arise, O LORD, in thine anger
If I have done this; if there be iniquity in my hands
questions.correctAnswer: O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust
questions.explanation: This phrase appears first in Psalms 7:1, which is the earliest verse among the options.

questions.question: Who is the Shiggaion in Psalms 7 sung unto?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:1 states that the Shiggaion of David was sung unto the LORD.

questions.question: From whom does David ask to be saved in Psalms 7:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:1 specifically says, 'save me from all them that persecute me.'

questions.question: What animal is used as a metaphor for tearing the soul in Psalms 7:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:2 uses the metaphor of a lion tearing the soul.

questions.question: What does David say there is none to do while the lion rends his soul?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:2 says 'while there is none to deliver.'

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to consider if there is iniquity in his hands?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:3 says, 'O LORD my God, if I have done this; if there be iniquity in my hands.'

questions.question: Who does David say he has delivered that was without cause his enemy?
options: Him that was at peace with me
questions.correctAnswer: Him that was at peace with me
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:4 states, 'yea, I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy.'

questions.question: What does David say his enemy may do to his soul in Psalms 7:5?
options: Persecute my soul and take it
Bless my soul and protect it
questions.correctAnswer: Persecute my soul and take it
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:5 says, 'Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take it.'

questions.question: Where does David say the enemy may lay his honour in Psalms 7:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:5 says, 'and lay mine honour in the dust.'

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to do in His anger in Psalms 7:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:6 says, 'Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself.'

questions.question: Why does David ask the LORD to awake in Psalms 7:6?
options: To the judgment that thou hast commanded
questions.correctAnswer: To the judgment that thou hast commanded
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:6 says, 'awake for me to the judgment that thou hast commanded.'

questions.question: David refers to Cush as belonging to which tribe?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:1 mentions 'Cush the Benjamite,' indicating Cush is from the tribe of Benjamin.

questions.question: David asks the LORD to save him from all those who persecute him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:1 says, 'save me from all them that persecute me.'

questions.question: David says that his enemies are like eagles tearing his soul.
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:2 uses the metaphor of a lion, not eagles, tearing the soul.

questions.question: David says he has rewarded evil to those who were peaceful towards him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:4 says, 'If I have rewarded evil unto him that was at peace with me,' implying he has not done so.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 7:8, how does the psalmist ask the LORD to judge him?
options: According to my righteousness and mine integrity
According to my wealth and power
According to the number of my deeds
questions.correctAnswer: According to my righteousness and mine integrity
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:8 says, 'judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity that is in me.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 7:9 promise will happen if the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end as commanded in Psalms 7:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:9 says, 'Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end; but establish the just,' which follows the command in Psalms 7:8 to judge the psalmist according to righteousness.

questions.question: What reason does Psalms 7:10 give for God being the psalmist's defense?
options: Because God saveth the upright in heart
Because God is slow to anger
Because God is mighty in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Because God saveth the upright in heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:10 states, 'My defence is of God, which saveth the upright in heart.'

questions.question: How do Psalms 7:11 and 7:12 connect in describing God's response to the wicked?
options: God is angry with the wicked daily and prepares to punish them if they do not repent
God ignores the wicked and blesses the righteous
God rewards the wicked and punishes the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God is angry with the wicked daily and prepares to punish them if they do not repent
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:11 says God is angry with the wicked every day, and 7:12 says if they do not turn, God will ready his sword and bow to punish them.

questions.question: What does Psalms 7:7 say the congregation of the people will do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:7 states, 'So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 7:11, how often is God angry with the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:11 clearly says, 'God is angry with the wicked every day.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 7:9 say God tries or tests in people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:9 states, 'for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.'

questions.question: What action does Psalms 7:12 describe God preparing if the wicked do not turn?
options: Whet his sword and ready his bow
Bring a flood upon the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Whet his sword and ready his bow
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:12 says, 'If he turn not, he will whet his sword; he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.'

questions.question: Why might the psalmist ask God to return on high according to Psalms 7:7?
options: For the sakes of the congregation of the people
questions.correctAnswer: For the sakes of the congregation of the people
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:7 says, 'for their sakes therefore return thou on high,' referring to the congregation that surrounds the psalmist.

questions.question: What does Psalm 7:10 imply about the character of those God saves?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:10 says God saves those who are 'upright in heart,' emphasizing integrity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 7:8 relate to the theme of integrity in Christian living?
options: It asks God to judge based on righteousness and integrity within
It encourages hiding faults from others
It emphasizes wealth as a sign of integrity
It promotes harsh judgment without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: It asks God to judge based on righteousness and integrity within
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:8 requests God to judge according to the psalmist's righteousness and internal integrity, highlighting inner faithfulness.

questions.question: What practical lesson about forgiveness can be derived from Psalms 7:9's call to end wickedness and establish the just?
options: God values justice but desires the wicked to cease their evil ways
God ignores wickedness and rewards the unjust
The wicked should be punished without chance of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God values justice but desires the wicked to cease their evil ways
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:9 balances ending wickedness with establishing the just, showing God's desire for repentance and justice.

questions.question: How does Psalms 7:11 encourage believers regarding God's view of daily struggles with wickedness?
options: God is consistently angry with the wicked and supports the righteous daily
God is indifferent to daily struggles
God only judges once in a lifetime
God favors the wicked over the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God is consistently angry with the wicked and supports the righteous daily
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:11 shows God's daily anger with wickedness, implying ongoing protection for the righteous.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 7:10 teaches that God saves those who are upright in heart.
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:10 says, 'My defence is of God, which saveth the upright in heart,' confirming this truth.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 7:12, God will ignore the wicked if they do not turn from their ways.
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:12 states that if the wicked do not turn, God will whet his sword and prepare to punish them, showing He does not ignore them.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 7.

questions.question: What instruments has God prepared for the wicked according to Psalms 7:13?
questions.explanation: God has prepared for him the instruments of death as stated in Psalms 7:13.

questions.question: What does the wicked bring forth according to Psalms 7:14?
questions.explanation: The verse states that he hath conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood (Psalms 7:14).

questions.question: What happens to the pit that the wicked has made according to Psalms 7:15?
questions.explanation: The verse explains that he made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made (Psalms 7:15).

questions.question: What does Psalms 7:16 say will happen to the wicked's mischief?
options: It shall return upon his own head
questions.correctAnswer: It shall return upon his own head
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:16 states that his mischief shall return upon his own head.

questions.question: How does the psalmist intend to praise the Lord according to Psalms 7:17?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness (Psalms 7:17).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'mischief' in Psalms 7:14?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'mischief' refers to wickedness or wrongdoing, which aligns with the context of the verse.

questions.question: What literary technique is used in the phrase 'His mischief shall return upon his own head' from Psalms 7:16?
questions.explanation: The phrase exemplifies parallelism, a common literary device in Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of divine judgment in Psalms 7:11?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 speaks of God's vengeance, echoing the theme of divine judgment found in Psalms 7:11.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of the wicked falling into their own traps as seen in Psalms 7:15?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:27 states that whoever digs a pit will fall into it, paralleling the theme in Psalms 7:15.

questions.question: What comes before the plea for deliverance in Psalms 7:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:1 begins with a declaration of trust in God for deliverance.

questions.question: What comes after the statement of God's righteousness in Psalms 7:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:17 concludes with a commitment to praise the Lord, serving as a call to worship.

questions.question: The term 'righteous' in Psalms 7:10 refers to what characteristic of God?
questions.explanation: The term 'righteous' in this context emphasizes God's justice and moral integrity as reflected in Psalms 7:10.

questions.question: The phrase 'God judgeth the righteous' in Psalms 7:11 indicates what aspect of God's character?
questions.explanation: This phrase emphasizes God's impartiality in judgment, as He judges both the righteous and the wicked (Psalms 7:11).

questions.question: It is true that Psalms 7 expresses themes of trust and divine justice.
questions.explanation: Psalms 7 clearly expresses themes of trust in God and His justice throughout the chapter.

questions.question: It is false that the psalmist blames God for his suffering in Psalms 7.
questions.explanation: The psalmist does not blame God; instead, he seeks refuge and justice from God amidst his suffering (Psalms 7:1).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 7:3 teach about human sin?
options: The necessity of self-examination for guilt before God
The inherent righteousness of man before God
The impossibility of humans committing iniquity
The universal forgiveness of sins without repentance
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of self-examination for guilt before God
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:3 says, "O LORD my God, if I have done this; if there be iniquity in my hands," showing David's practice of examining his own guilt before appealing to God.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 7:9 teach about God's judgment?
options: God tests the hearts and reins to distinguish the just from the wicked
God is indifferent to human righteousness
God judges only outward actions, not inner motives
God's judgment is arbitrary and unpredictable
questions.correctAnswer: God tests the hearts and reins to distinguish the just from the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:9 states, "for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins," indicating God's thorough judgment of inner motives.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 7:14 teach about human sin and its consequences?
options: Evil conceived in the heart leads to falsehood and judgment upon oneself
Sin is inconsequential and can be ignored
Falsehood is unrelated to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: Evil conceived in the heart leads to falsehood and judgment upon oneself
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:14 describes one who "travaileth with iniquity, and hath conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood," showing sinful intent leading to destructive consequences.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 7:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:11 says, "God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day," indicating God's attribute of wrath against sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 7:10 specifically demonstrate?
options: God's providential defense of the upright
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential defense of the upright
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:10 declares, "My defence is of God, which saveth the upright in heart," showing God's protective providence.

questions.question: How does Psalms 7:6 connect to broader scriptural themes of divine justice?
options: It anticipates the final judgment where God arises in anger against evil
It promotes human vengeance over divine justice
It denies God's involvement in human affairs
It suggests God delays judgment indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the final judgment where God arises in anger against evil
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:6 calls on God to "Arise...because of the rage of mine enemies," reflecting the biblical theme of God actively judging evil (cf. Revelation 19:11).

questions.question: How does Psalms 7:17 relate to the doctrine of worship in the context of divine righteousness?
options: It affirms that praise flows from recognizing God's righteousness
It separates worship from ethical considerations
It limits praise to private, not communal, settings
It denies the importance of God's character in worship
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that praise flows from recognizing God's righteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:17 says, "I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness," showing worship as a response to God's just character.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 7:8 and Psalms 7:9 teach about God's judgment?
options: God judges based on righteousness and tests the heart to discern true integrity
God judges arbitrarily without regard to righteousness
God only judges external actions without insight into the heart
God's judgment is delayed until after death exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: God judges based on righteousness and tests the heart to discern true integrity
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:8 requests judgment "according to my righteousness," and 7:9 emphasizes God "trieth the hearts and reins," combining external and internal judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 7:12 and Psalms 7:13 teach about God's judgment and instruments of justice?
options: God actively prepares instruments of judgment against the unrepentant
God is passive and does not execute judgment
God uses human methods exclusively for justice
God forgives without any consequences for sin
questions.correctAnswer: God actively prepares instruments of judgment against the unrepentant
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:12-13 depict God "whetting his sword," and preparing "arrows against the persecutors," showing divine readiness to judge.

questions.question: What combined theological doctrine do Psalms 7:15 and Psalms 7:16 teach about the principle of divine retribution?
options: Those who plot evil will fall into their own snares and suffer their own violence
Evil plans always succeed without consequence
Retribution is random and unrelated to actions
questions.correctAnswer: Those who plot evil will fall into their own snares and suffer their own violence
questions.explanation: Verses 7:15-16 describe the evildoer "falling into the ditch which he made" and his mischief "return upon his own head," illustrating divine retribution.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 7:11-13 promotes a harsh, vindictive God. What does Psalms 7:11-13 actually teach?
options: God is righteously angry with persistent wickedness and prepares just judgment accordingly
God is cruel and punishes without cause
God's anger is arbitrary and unregulated
God punishes even the repentant immediately
questions.correctAnswer: God is righteously angry with persistent wickedness and prepares just judgment accordingly
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:11-13 show God's anger is directed at unrepentant wickedness, with preparation for judgment as a just response.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 7:4 teach about the believer's response to enemies?
options: Believers are called to deliver even those who become enemies without cause
Believers should repay evil with evil
Believers are justified in seeking revenge
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to deliver even those who become enemies without cause
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:4 says, "yea, I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy," indicating a commitment to mercy despite enmity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 7:1 specifically demonstrate?
options: God as a refuge and deliverer
questions.correctAnswer: God as a refuge and deliverer
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:1 says, "O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me," demonstrating trust in God’s deliverance and refuge.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 7:2 and Psalms 7:5 teach about the believer's vulnerability and trust in divine justice?
options: Believers may face severe persecution but can entrust their cause to God
Trust in God removes all earthly suffering
Believers should rely solely on human defense
questions.correctAnswer: Believers may face severe persecution but can entrust their cause to God
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:2 and 7:5 describe threats of soul being torn and life trodden down, yet the psalmist appeals to God for deliverance and justice.

questions.question: How does Psalms 7:7 relate to the corporate nature of God's people in worship and justice?
options: It shows the congregation surrounds God, indicating communal involvement in His justice
It denies any role for the congregation in divine matters
It suggests worship is only private and hidden
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the congregation surrounds God, indicating communal involvement in His justice
questions.explanation: Psalms 7:7 says, "So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about," reflecting the corporate nature of God's people in worship and justice.
